page: Amazon Web Services t8i.small is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the t8i burstable performance family. It is powered by an Intel processor operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, utilizing the Nitro hypervisor. The instance is provisioned with 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 1.0 GB per core.

This instance does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps, indicating that network throughput is heavily throttled or relies entirely on burst allocation. There are no integrated GPU accelerators. The lack of local storage and low baseline network performance represent significant tradeoffs, positioning this instance for workloads with minimal external data transfer requirements.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t8i.small is designed as a budget-friendly entry-level option within the burstable hardware class. It is structured for low-intensity, intermittent workloads rather than sustained high-throughput computation. Appropriate workloads include lightweight microservices, basic development or testing environments, low-traffic web serving, and simple automation scripts that do not require continuous CPU utilization or high network bandwidth.
